name: Do in-law suites need separate utilities in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do in-law suites need separate utilities in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Do in-law suites need separate utilities in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Separate utilities are not always required, but they can change how the suite functions and how much the project costs. Shared utilities are often simpler for conversions or smaller units, while separate service can make a detached suite feel more independent. The decision affects electrical capacity, water lines, sewer routing, and possible meter changes. Utility planning should happen early because retrofitting is often more expensive than designing it into the project from the start. Homeowners should also consider how the suite will be used in the future, since utility setup can influence occupancy flexibility and operating costs. A good contractor will evaluate existing service capacity before plans are finalized.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not always. Some in-law suites share utilities with the main house, while others are designed with separate meters or dedicated service depending on project scope and city requirements. Utility choice affects cost, resale, billing, and how independent the unit feels. The right setup depends on the unit type and intended use.
